summary: I ʕəmḏo has the baptized participant as subject; III active has a baptizer and a patient (zero nominal or suffix), while overt III Detransitive mtaʕmiḏi places recipients as subject. English or German semantic voice does not determine morphology (94/48).
JTM 4.2 consistently uses b əšme d Mšiḥo as the naming formula. In 94/48 b- marks water and chrism instead. These transparent ritual frames do not require a separate idiom or sense.

Inherited tuʕmiḏo is retained in III Detransitive Infinitiv by the entry's convention. Its nominal task/genitive contexts do not require a passive interpretation. ʕamaḏe and ʕmoḏo are held outside firm new verbal boxes pending morphological verification.
The active person title Maʕməḏono belongs with Part act.; the inherited spelling Maʕmiḏono and its references are preserved by moving the existing example rather than rewriting it.

I ʕaməḏ has the baptism recipient as subject; III mʕaməḏ-/maʕmaḏ- has a baptizer and patient. Retain I under the entry’s receptive sense sich taufen lassen without changing the original base forms; the new Preterit Intransitive box is provisional.

Jan 1.7/133–134 shows l-marked questioned/cleft baptizers with patient suffixes, beside the unmarked nominal agent u ǧəddo. These are active III forms, despite English passive paraphrases being possible.
Reduced mʕaməḏ-/mʕamaḏ- and fuller maʕmaḏ- alternate without evidence for another stem. The broken quote in mʕamaḏ”ox at Jan 2.5/1531 cannot establish a publishable unusual form.
Cross-baptism is ritual participant extension; conversion follows baptism in Jan 2.21/3927, but this result does not establish an independent meaning convert.

Infectum may show an event in progress, a promise with gəd-, or prospective baptism subject to registration requirements. Infectum-wa at Jan 2.21/3934 gives habitual circumvention of those requirements.
The human title Maʕmiḏono remains moved to Part act. as proposed in round 1; the human-readable counts apply that move without repeating it in this round’s JSON.
